run1.note: The first run, commit cc08c7bd1626377096a820a9ed5146931e82b1f6. G7 and G8 failed there partly from a prototype optimiser defect: the profile fits over rho and the blend were stuck above the oracle chi-square, so intervals were spuriously narrow (29 of 53 value-returning G7 fits agreed with the oracle, against 53 of 56 in the second run). The optimiser was repaired (warm and rho-scaled cold starts, a descending pass) with no bound or amendment changed and the legs re-run; this first run stays on record. Its G3 row measured the flux ratio against the oracle numerical Jacobian only (1.66e-7); the second run reports the closed-form comparison beside it.

readings.G8: The runner required every event flagged blend-degenerate (98) to carry a tE range (95), a rule stricter than the committed sentence and AM3, which count events returned blend-degenerate with a tE range: 95 of 100 = 0.95, above the 0.9 bound. The row is recorded as the run produced it (fail) and is not re-run or re-labelled after the result; the literal reading is a pass and does not change the verdict (C), since G3 and G7 fail. Which reading is the record is a question for Carl.
readings.G3: G1 to G5 are exact to 1e-14 or better against the closed forms; G3 fails against the oracle only, because the oracle pins its magnifications by finite differences (about 1e-7 noise), so the committed 1e-9 on that comparison cannot be met by any code. The kernel agrees with the closed forms to 3.6e-16. The leg stays failing.
readings.G7: The profile minimum is still above the oracle scipy fit by more than 1 in chi-square for 36 of 200 events, so the prototype optimiser is not yet the oracle one; the coverage 0.286 and 0.446 are against the committed bands [0.610, 0.750] and [0.917, 0.983]. Far events (u0 above 3 rho) return a value in 2 of 100 cases, as the leg requires of unconstrained rho.
